# Machine shop guides

> Free tools for small machine shops: a CMMC Level 1 self-assessment checklist (the 15 FAR 52.204-21 requirements judged by their 59 NIST SP 800-171A objectives, met, not met or N/A, with an evidence worksheet), a CMMC scoping worksheet that sorts a shop's assets into the 32 CFR 170.19 categories, a DFARS 252.204-7012 cyber incident checklist (72-hour report deadline, 90-day image hold), a stock-size reader for STEP and STL files (bounding box, round bar, stock to cut and a first cycle time from the shop's own feeds, in the browser), an SPRS score calculator for the 110 NIST SP 800-171 requirements (DoD Assessment Methodology, 110 minus 5/3/1 per gap), a NIST 800-171 system security plan (SSP) template that builds the SSP and POA&M in the browser, a job-shop quote calculator from the shop's own rates that also writes the customer quote, a quoted-vs-actual hours check that turns the shop's job history into calibration factors, and guides to CMMC Level 1 vs Level 2, SSPs and POA&Ms, and pricing a machined part.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, compliance, financial or engineering advice. A calculated score is a self-check, not a CMMC assessment or certification; not affiliated with or endorsed by the DoD. CMMC status on the pages was checked 24 November 2026 (Phase 2 suspended since 13 July 2026).

## Tools

- [CMMC Level 1 self-assessment checklist](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-level-1-self-assessment.html): 15 requirements word for word from FAR 52.204-21(b)(1); 59 objectives from NIST SP 800-171A mapped by Table 2 to 32 CFR 170.15, FCI read for CUI; MET or NOT MET in its entirety (32 CFR 170.24(c)(1)); N/A counts as met.
- [CMMC scoping worksheet](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-scoping-worksheet.html): list assets (workstations, CAM, DNC, CNC controllers, CMM, printers, phones, cloud mail and file services, MSP tools) and answer a few questions each; the category the answers point to under 32 CFR 170.19 table 3 (CUI Asset, Security Protection Asset, Contractor Risk Managed Asset, Specialized Asset, Out-of-Scope) or Level 1 paragraph (b); outside services by table 4 (CUI or Security Protection Data, cloud or not); what each must have documented; open items (a CRMA with no written policy, out-of-scope with no separation); asset inventory CSV, SSP inventory lines and a saved file (JSON) that the planned CMMC workspace imports; rule text read 25 Nov 2026; nothing uploaded.
- [SPRS score calculator](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/sprs-score-calculator.html): 110 minus 5/3/1 per gap; the CMMC Level 2 Conditional check (88 points, POA&M-eligible gaps only, and the six requirements 32 CFR 170.21(a)(2)(iii) never allows on a POA&M); POA&M starter CSV marking each gap allowed or not.
- [NIST 800-171 SSP template](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/nist-800-171-ssp-template.html): system security plan builder in the browser; system boundary, environment, connections, users; status, implementation statement, owner, evidence and provider for each of the 110 requirements; review of what 3.12.4 still needs and rows an assessor would return; SSP as HTML or Markdown, POA&M as CSV, plan file as JSON; nothing uploaded.
- [DFARS 252.204-7012 cyber incident reporting checklist](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/dfars-7012-incident-reporting.html): 72-hour DIBNet report deadline from discovery (paragraph (a), "rapidly report"); image and packet-capture hold of at least 90 days from report submission (paragraph (e)); steps (c) to (m) with paragraph cites, including DC3 malware submission, medium assurance certificate, subcontractor report number to the higher tier, cloud provider duties; incident record as Markdown or JSON; clause version MAY 2024; nothing uploaded.
- [CMMC affirmation due dates](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-affirmation-dates.html): enter the CMMC Status Date, the level (Level 1 Self, Level 2 Self, Level 2 C3PAO), Final or Conditional, and the last SPRS affirmation; the annual affirmation (32 CFR 170.22(a), after every assessment including POA&M closeout and annually thereafter), the 180-day POA&M closeout deadline from a Conditional status date (170.16(a)(1)(ii)(B), 170.17), the next assessment (yearly at Level 1, every three years at Level 2, not restarted by a closeout), a year-by-year plan, an .ics calendar file with alarms 60 and 7 days ahead, Markdown and JSON; nothing uploaded.
- [Stock size from a STEP or STL file](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/stock-size-from-step-file.html): drop a customer's model; bounding box (exact for planes, cylinders and cones, otherwise a stated upper bound), smallest round bar along each axis, rectangular and round stock with your allowance, facing, cut-off and rounding; weight and material cost from your density and price; from an STL, a first cycle time (metal removed ÷ your width × depth × feed, plus surface area ÷ your finishing stepover × feed, your allowance and load/unload), handed with the material cost to the quote calculator; STEP units read from the file; parts modelled at an angle boxed square to their own faces; read in the browser, never uploaded.
- [Job-shop quote calculator](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/job-shop-quote-calculator.html): material, setup, programming, cycle time, other operations and markup from the shop's own rates at each quantity break; optional setup and cycle-time calibration factors; then a customer quote to send (price each and extended per quantity, part number and revision, lead time, validity, terms, notes and exclusions, without the cost lines), downloaded as HTML or copied as email text, with a check of what a buyer would send back.
- [RFQ review checklist](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/rfq-review.html): paste an RFQ; finds part numbers, revisions, quantities and annual usage, material, finish, tolerances (tight ones flagged against the shop's own line), quote-due and delivery dates, 13 FAR/DFARS clauses by number with their official titles (52.204-21, 252.204-7012, -7019, -7020, -7021, 252.225-7009, -7048, 252.246-7007, -7008, 52.246-2, -11, -15, 52.211-15), CUI, ITAR/EAR, AS9102, certs, NADCAP and DPAS markers; questions for the buyer as an email; review CSV; quantities into the quote calculator. Pattern matching in the browser; nothing uploaded.
- [Drawing review](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/drawing-review.html): drop a part drawing PDF (exported from CAD, with a text layer); reads the title block (part number, drawing number, revision, title, material, finish, scale, sheet, CAGE code) with the text each value came from, the latest row of the revision table and whether it matches the title block, the general tolerance block (by decimal places, angles with minutes, fractions, ISO 2768 class, units, Y14.5 edition), numbered notes with continuation lines tagged by cost (finish, heat treat, marking, deburr, inspection, certs, controlled data) and gaps in their numbering, dimension and thread callouts in the views, distribution statements B-F, CUI and export markings; writes the questions for the buyer as an email, a CSV, and hands the callouts and general tolerances to the first article checker in the link (the list in the # part, never sent to a server). Scans and dimensions drawn as lines cannot be read, and it says so. In the browser; nothing uploaded.
- [First article inspection checker](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/first-article-inspection.html): paste the FAI characteristic table (balloon number, requirement as written, results, tooling, NCR); reads bilateral, unequal, limit, MAX/MIN, surface finish, geometric tolerances (0 to the tolerance; MMC bonus not added), basic and reference dimensions, threads and notes, and bare nominals against the title block general tolerance; judges every result, flags out of tolerance, no NCR on a reject, blank results, skipped or repeated balloon numbers, fewer results than places, pass marks where a value can be measured, readings near a limit; downloads an AS9102 Form 3 style CSV. In the browser; nothing uploaded. AS9102 itself is an SAE standard and is not reproduced.
- [Quoted vs actual hours](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/quote-vs-actual.html): paste a job history CSV (quoted and actual setup hours and cycle minutes, machine, quantity, won/lost); per machine, the median actual-to-quoted ratio, middle half, share of jobs over quote, quantity-weighted hours missed and their cost at the shop's rate, win rate, outlier jobs, and a correction factor (offered at 5+ jobs, "rough" under 15) that fills the quote calculator. No benchmarks; nothing uploaded.

## Guides

- [CMMC Level 1 vs Level 2 for a small machine shop](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-level-1-vs-level-2.html)
- [CMMC flow-down to subcontractors and suppliers](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-subcontractor-flow-down.html): the level each supplier needs under 32 CFR 170.23 (FCI only: Level 1 (Self); CUI: Level 2 (Self) at least, Level 2 (C3PAO) when the prime contract requires C3PAO or Level 3), quoted word for word; DFARS 252.204-7021 (NOV 2025) paragraphs (d)(1)(ii), (d)(4), (f)(1) (COTS excluded, (e)(1) left out) and (f)(2) (check current status before award); what "current" means (1 year, 3 years, 180 days Conditional, affirmation within 1 year); read on eCFR 27 Nov 2026
- [What goes in an SSP and a POA&M](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/ssp-and-poam.html)
- [How to price a machined part](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/how-to-price-a-machined-part.html)
- [Machine shop quoting software: the four kinds and how to choose](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/machine-shop-quoting-software.html): spreadsheet, ERP quoting module, standalone quoting platform, AI RFQ reader; listed prices with their sources as of 24 Nov 2026 (QuotedPart, JobBOSS², ProShop; none confirmed for Paperless Parts or the AI entrants); demo questions, including CUI drawings and DFARS 252.204-7012(b)(2)(ii)(D)

## Answers

The questions each page answers in its "Common questions" section, with the answer as the page states it. Each link opens that section; the page has the sources.

- [What is an SPRS score and how is it calculated?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/#faq): It is the NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment score a contractor posts in the Supplier Performance Risk System. You start at 110 and subtract 5, 3 or 1 point for each of the 110 requirements not met. The SPRS score calculator here does that arithmetic, with the partial credit for MFA and FIPS cryptography.
- [Do I need CMMC Level 1 or Level 2?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/#faq): It depends on what the contract sends you. Federal Contract Information (FCI) only, under FAR 52.204-21, means Level 1: 15 requirements and a yearly self-assessment. Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), such as a drawing marked CUI, puts the systems that touch it in Level 2 scope: the 110 requirements of NIST SP 800-171.
- [How do I price a machined part?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/#faq): From your own records: a shop rate built from your books, material per part from the stock price and yield, setup and programming spread over the lot, cycle time at the machine rate, secondary and outside operations, then markup. Re-run it at each quantity for the price breaks. The job-shop quote calculator does the arithmetic and ships no rates of its own.
- [Is anything I type uploaded?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/#faq): No. Every tool on these pages runs in your browser; drawings, models, RFQs and answers are not uploaded. Some pages can keep a draft in your browser if you turn that on.
- [How often does a CMMC affirmation have to be made?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-affirmation-dates.html#faq): After every assessment, including a POA&M closeout, and annually thereafter (32 CFR 170.22(a)). The Affirming Official enters each one in SPRS. This page counts the year from the latest affirmation you enter.
- [How long do I have to close out a Conditional CMMC Level 2 status?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-affirmation-dates.html#faq): 180 days from the Conditional CMMC Status Date. For Level 2 (Self) the closeout self-assessment is posted to SPRS within that time; for Level 2 (C3PAO) a C3PAO performs the closeout assessment. If the 180 days pass without a closeout, the Conditional status expires.
- [When is the next CMMC assessment due?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-affirmation-dates.html#faq): A year after the CMMC Status Date for Level 1 (Self), and three years after it for Level 2, by yourself or by a C3PAO. A POA&M closeout does not restart the three years: they count from the original status date.
- [What are the CMMC Level 1 requirements?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-level-1-self-assessment.html#faq): The 15 safeguarding requirements of FAR 52.204-21(b)(1)(i) to (xv). 32 CFR 170.14(c)(2) makes them the CMMC Level 1 requirements, and each is judged against its NIST SP 800-171A assessment objectives, 59 in all, reading FCI wherever an objective says CUI.
- [Does CMMC Level 1 have a score or a POA&M?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-level-1-self-assessment.html#faq): No. Each requirement is met or not met in its entirety, there is no point score, and 32 CFR 170.21 allows no plan of action and milestones at Level 1. Every one of the 15 has to be met before you claim the level.
- [How often is the Level 1 self-assessment done?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-level-1-self-assessment.html#faq): Every year. The result goes into SPRS with the level, date, scope and CAGE codes, and an Affirming Official affirms compliance at the end of each self-assessment and every year after (32 CFR 170.22).
- [What is the difference between CMMC Level 1 and Level 2?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-level-1-vs-level-2.html#faq): Level 1 is the 15 basic requirements of FAR 52.204-21, self-assessed every year, met or not met with no score. Level 2 is the 110 requirements of NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2, scored from 110 down, assessed every three years by yourself or by a C3PAO, with an annual affirmation.
- [How do I know if my shop handles CUI or only FCI?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-level-1-vs-level-2.html#faq): The contract tells you. Look for DFARS 252.204-7012, 7019, 7020 and 7021 in your purchase orders and flow-downs, and for drawings or models that arrive marked CUI. If every contract only involves FCI, such as purchase orders and delivery schedules, you are looking at Level 1.
- [Is CMMC Phase 2 suspended?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-level-1-vs-level-2.html#faq): As of 24 November 2026, yes. Phase 2, which would have required C3PAO Level 2 certification from 10 November 2026, was suspended by the Department of War on 13 July 2026. Self-assessments, DFARS 252.204-7012 and the SPRS score requirements of 7019 and 7020 still apply.
- [What are the CMMC asset categories?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-scoping-worksheet.html#faq): For Level 2, 32 CFR 170.19 sorts every asset into five: CUI Assets, Security Protection Assets, Contractor Risk Managed Assets, Specialized Assets and Out-of-Scope Assets. Each has its own documentation and assessment requirements.
- [Are CNC controllers in CMMC scope?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-scoping-worksheet.html#faq): Usually as Specialized Assets: equipment that can process CUI but cannot be fully secured, such as operational technology and test equipment. They are documented and managed under your risk-based policies, but not assessed against the other requirements. At Level 1, Specialized Assets are not part of the assessment scope.
- [Why scope before writing the SSP?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/cmmc-scoping-worksheet.html#faq): Every asset you put in scope as a CUI Asset has to meet all 110 requirements and becomes a line in the SSP and the SPRS score. A small enclave, such as one mailbox, one share, two workstations and the shop-floor machines as Specialized Assets, is often far less work than securing the whole office.
- [How long do I have to report a cyber incident under DFARS 252.204-7012?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/dfars-7012-incident-reporting.html#faq): 72 hours from discovery. The clause defines "rapidly report" as within 72 hours of discovery of any cyber incident, and the report is filed at dibnet.dod.mil. The clock starts at discovery, not when your review ends.
- [How long must I keep images after an incident?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/dfars-7012-incident-reporting.html#faq): At least 90 days from submitting the cyber incident report, under paragraph (e): images of the affected systems and the relevant monitoring and packet capture data. The 90 days start at the report, not at discovery.
- [What do I need before I can file on DIBNet?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/dfars-7012-incident-reporting.html#faq): A DoD-approved medium assurance certificate, obtained through the External Certification Authority program (paragraph (c)(3)). Get it before an incident, not inside the 72 hours.
- [What should I check on a part drawing before quoting?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/drawing-review.html#faq): The title block (part number, revision, material, finish), whether the revision table's last row matches it, the general tolerance block, every numbered note, the tightest tolerances and surface finishes, and any distribution or export marking.
- [What does "unless otherwise specified" mean on a drawing?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/drawing-review.html#faq): It sets the tolerance for every dimension with none of its own, usually by decimal places, plus angles and sometimes fractions; an ISO 2768 class uses that standard's tables instead. It often decides the machine and the inspection, because it covers most of the part.
- [What do distribution statements on a drawing mean?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/drawing-review.html#faq): Statement A means approved for public release; B to F limit distribution, so check before forwarding the drawing to a plating or heat-treat house. A CUI marking means the systems holding the file must meet NIST SP 800-171.
- [What is a first article inspection?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/first-article-inspection.html#faq): A full inspection of one part made by the production process, to show the process can make the part to the drawing before the lot runs. Aerospace and defense customers usually ask for it in the AS9102 format: Form 1 part number accountability, Form 2 product accountability, Form 3 characteristic accountability.
- [When is a first article inspection required?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/first-article-inspection.html#faq): Normally on a new part, and again after a change that could affect it: the design, the process or source, the inspection method, the tooling or the location. A partial FAI covers only what the change touched. Lapses in production differ by customer, so the PO clauses and quality manual decide.
- [What gets an FAI report rejected?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/first-article-inspection.html#faq): A characteristic with no balloon or no result, "accept" written where a value can be measured, a result out of limits with no nonconformance number, fewer results than places on a multi-place feature, and missing certificates or a revision mismatch on Forms 1 and 2.
- [How do I work out a machine shop rate?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/how-to-price-a-machined-part.html#faq): From your books: the year's overhead (rent, utilities, insurance, software, equipment payments or depreciation, indirect wages) plus direct labour, divided by the hours you actually bill, not the hours the doors are open. Many shops keep separate rates per machine type.
- [How do I calculate material cost per part?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/how-to-price-a-machined-part.html#faq): Take the price of the stock form you will buy and divide by the number of parts one unit yields after saw kerf, facing stock, unusable remnant and workholding grip, then add an allowance for setup pieces and rejects.
- [How should outside processes go on a quote?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/how-to-price-a-machined-part.html#faq): Outside processes such as plating, anodizing or heat treatment usually carry a per-part price and a lot minimum. For short runs the minimum is what you pay, so quote it as a flat charge per lot rather than burying it in the part price.
- [How do job shops calculate a quote?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/job-shop-quote-calculator.html#faq): Material, setup, programming, cycle time, secondary operations and markup, from the shop's own rates. This calculator adds those lines and spreads the once-per-lot costs over the quantity, then shows the price per part at every quantity break.
- [Why does a small quantity cost more per part?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/job-shop-quote-calculator.html#faq): Setup, programming and any flat lot charge are paid once per lot. Spread over 5 parts they add far more to each part than spread over 100, so the quantity breaks are arithmetic, not a discount schedule.
- [What is the difference between markup and margin?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/job-shop-quote-calculator.html#faq): Markup is on cost: price = cost × (1 + markup). Margin is on price. A 25% markup on cost is a 20% margin on price.
- [What kinds of machine shop quoting software are there?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/machine-shop-quoting-software.html#faq): Four: a spreadsheet or calculator, the quoting module inside a job-shop ERP, a standalone quoting platform, and the newer AI RFQ readers that draft the parts and operations from the email, drawing and model for an estimator to check. Each needs your own rates before it gives a good number.
- [How much does machine shop quoting software cost?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/machine-shop-quoting-software.html#faq): Public listings checked on 24 November 2026 showed QuotedPart at $199 a month per shop (Toolradar), JobBOSS² at about $3,000 a year (SoftwareConnect) and ProShop at $650 to $715 a month (G2). We could confirm no public price for Paperless Parts or the AI quoting entrants. Listings disagree, so get the current price from the vendor.
- [Can I upload CUI drawings to a quoting tool?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/machine-shop-quoting-software.html#faq): Only to a service that may hold them. Under DFARS 252.204-7012(b)(2)(ii)(D), a cloud service that stores covered defense information for you must meet security requirements equivalent to the FedRAMP Moderate baseline. Ask the vendor in writing, and keep CUI and export-controlled drawings out of any tool that says no.
- [What does a NIST 800-171 SSP need to include?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/nist-800-171-ssp-template.html#faq): Requirement 3.12.4 asks for the system boundaries, the environments of operation, how each security requirement is implemented, and the relationships with or connections to other systems. NIST prescribes no format; this template lays it out as contacts, the system, a summary, one entry per requirement and the POA&M.
- [Can I get an SPRS score without an SSP?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/nist-800-171-ssp-template.html#faq): No. The DoD Assessment Methodology says an assessment cannot be completed without a system security plan, which is why 3.12.4 has no point value but blocks the score.
- [What date do I post in SPRS for reaching 110?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/nist-800-171-ssp-template.html#faq): A Basic assessment asks for the date you expect to reach 110. The template takes it from the latest milestone date on your POA&M gaps, and only when every gap has one.
- [How do I compare quoted and actual hours?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/quote-vs-actual.html#faq): Export the job cost or estimate-vs-actual report from your ERP, or keep the same columns from travelers and the time clock, and paste it here. The page shows, per machine, the median of actual ÷ quoted, the hours missed and what they cost at your rate.
- [What is a quote correction factor?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/quote-vs-actual.html#faq): The median ratio of actual to quoted hours on a machine: 1.20 means the typical job took 20% longer than quoted. The job-shop quote calculator multiplies your setup and cycle-time estimates by it. It is offered with at least 5 jobs and called rough below 15.
- [Why use the median instead of the average?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/quote-vs-actual.html#faq): So one scrapped-and-rerun job does not move every future quote. Jobs that took more than twice, or under half, the quoted time are listed separately as worth a look.
- [What should I check in an RFQ before quoting?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/rfq-review.html#faq): Part numbers and drawing revisions, lot sizes and annual usage, material and finish specs, the tightest tolerances, the quote and delivery dates, and the FAR and DFARS clauses that add cost or decide whether you can take the job. Whatever is missing becomes a question for the buyer.
- [Which DFARS clauses matter for a machine shop?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/rfq-review.html#faq): 252.204-7012 (protecting CUI to NIST SP 800-171), 252.204-7019 and -7020 (a current SPRS score), 252.204-7021 (a CMMC level), 252.225-7009 (specialty metals) and 252.225-7048 (export control), alongside FAR 52.246-11 (a named quality standard) and 52.211-15 (DPAS-rated orders).
- [Do ISO 9001 and AS9100 require contract review?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/rfq-review.html#faq): Both ask for a review of the requirements before you commit to supply, in clause 8.2.3 (review of the requirements for products and services).
- [How is the SPRS score calculated?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/sprs-score-calculator.html#faq): The NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Methodology starts at 110 and subtracts 5, 3 or 1 point for each requirement not implemented, using the weights in its Annex A. The lowest possible score is minus 203.
- [What is the minimum SPRS score for CMMC Conditional Level 2?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/sprs-score-calculator.html#faq): 88, which is 80% of 110, under 32 CFR 170.21, and every open item must be one the rule allows on a POA&M: in general 1-point requirements only, plus 3.13.11 at its 3-point partial value. Six requirements can never be left open: 3.1.20, 3.1.22, 3.12.4, 3.10.3, 3.10.4 and 3.10.5.
- [Which requirements get partial credit?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/sprs-score-calculator.html#faq): Two. 3.5.3 multifactor authentication costs 3 points instead of 5 when MFA covers only remote and privileged users, and 3.13.11 costs 3 instead of 5 when CUI is encrypted but the module is not FIPS-validated. 3.12.4, the system security plan, has no points, but without it no score can be completed.
- [What is the difference between an SSP and a POA&M?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/ssp-and-poam.html#faq): The system security plan says what your system is and how each NIST SP 800-171 requirement is met (requirement 3.12.4). The plan of action and milestones says how and when you will close what is not met (requirement 3.12.2).
- [What can be left on a POA&M for CMMC Level 2?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/ssp-and-poam.html#faq): Under 32 CFR 170.21: a score of at least 88 of 110, generally only 1-point requirements open (plus 3.13.11 at its 3-point partial value), never 3.1.20, 3.1.22, 3.12.4, 3.10.3, 3.10.4 or 3.10.5, and everything closed by a closeout assessment within 180 days. Level 1 allows no POA&M at all.
- [What goes in a POA&M row?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/ssp-and-poam.html#faq): The requirement, the weakness as you found it, the planned action, who is responsible, the resources needed, milestone dates and the current status. NIST does not prescribe a format.
- [How do I find the stock size from a STEP file?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/stock-size-from-step-file.html#faq): Drop the .step, .stp or .stl file on this page. It works out the part's bounding box, the round bar it would turn from, and the stock to cut with your allowance per side, facing and cut-off, and rounding. The file is read in your browser and never uploaded.
- [How accurate is the bounding box?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/stock-size-from-step-file.html#faq): For STEP it reads the solid's edges, so faces on planes, cylinders and cones give the exact box; spheres, fillets and free-form surfaces get a containing shape and a warning. Checked against OpenCascade on 68 parts, it never gave a box smaller than the part, 60 were exact and the rest were at most 2.8 mm too large and flagged.
- [Can it estimate cycle time?](https://marisstella.app/machine-shop-guides/stock-size-from-step-file.html#faq): As a first number, from your own cutting data: roughing time is the metal to remove divided by your removal rate, finishing time is the surface area divided by your stepover times feed, plus your non-cutting allowance. It knows nothing about holes, threads or setups, so treat it as a starting line.
